notes: All 13 evals whose assertions were rewritten, plus review-changes eval 1 to verify the delegation fix. review-auth was unchanged and not re-run.
Not comparable to detection-skills-benchmark.json: the assertions changed, and this run removed the hooks, plugins, global skills and in-repo skill symlinks that contaminated the previous baselines.

VERIFIED FIX — audit-secrets masking: the with_skill arm masked all three secrets everywhere including in the sentence dismissing the AWS documentation example, the exact failure from iteration 1. All three baselines printed secrets in full, two of them inside a filter-repo --replace-text command.

VERIFIED FIX — review-changes delegation: the with_skill arm now says the auth guard 'needs a dedicated auth review (review-auth)'. This assertion failed in BOTH arms in iteration 1 because the handoff was only in the description.

VERIFIED FIX — review-migration lock semantics: both arms described the non-concurrent CREATE INDEX as a SHARE/write-blocking lock and the 40M-row UPDATE as a long transaction rather than a table lock. The iteration-1 assertions marked both arms failed on exactly this correct output.

REGRESSION — review-migration eval 1 assertion 5: the with_skill arm flags a nullable ADD COLUMN as a [medium] ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock risk while the baseline correctly ignores it. The Step 3 rewrite lists 'ALTER TABLE (most variants)' under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE without noting that a metadata-only ADD COLUMN holds it for milliseconds, overriding the risk table's Low rating.

REGRESSION — audit-dependencies eval 2: the skill scores BELOW baseline (4/6 vs 6/6). Its full-report format buries the answer to a pointed one-question prompt under two unrequested vite CVE findings sourced from model memory rather than supplied audit output, and asserts 'License risks (0) ... all clear' without data.

check-query-safety eval 1 still discriminates on nothing: all six assertions pass in both arms. Its rewrite kept detection and fix-shape assertions but added no structure, severity or restraint axis the baseline would miss.

Two assertions fail in both arms and are candidates for revision: review-migration eval 3 assertion 5 (both arms note a missing index on audit_logs.actor_id, which is defensible reviewing) and review-changes eval 1 assertion 3 (neither arm mentioned test coverage this run; the with_skill arm did in iteration 1, so this may be run-to-run variance rather than a bad assertion).
